messages:
maria: heads up — saw a pattern in staging: coalescer churning tenants with bursty short requests, then our deprioritization path kicks in and we see 300–800ms tail spikes for those tenants. can we discuss tradeoffs?

sam: ugh saw that in the canary too. looks like eviction windows are misaligned with the coalesce window so we repeatedly evict+rehydrate KV state.

jon: agree. two obvious options: (1) extend lease/grace so KV survives a few churn cycles, (2) move to soft-deprioritization where we keep KV but mark slots as low-prio and reduce batch size.

maria: option (1) reduces thrash but increases memory headroom pressure. option (2) keeps memory but hurts throughput for others if we don't enforce credits. tradeoffs: memory vs stable latency.

tia: can we do a hybrid? short bursts -> soft-deprio, repeated bursts -> eviction. something like a hysteresis counter per tenant.

lee: +1 to hysteresis. also we should align the eviction tick with coalesce windows to avoid evicting mid-window. small config sketch: 
```
coalescer:
  window_ms: 12
  eviction_grace_windows: 3   # allow 3 windows of churn
  soft_deprio_threshold: 5    # requests per window to trigger deprio
  deprio_batch_weight: 0.2
```

sam: nice. also consider KV-prefetch on soft-deprio re-entry: if a tenant is deprioritized frequently we might prefetch into a lightweight cache so rehydrate cost is lower.

jon: prefetch helps but io/memory trade offs again. curious: how often are we seeing churn? logs: 
```
[coalescer] tenant=acme bursts=7 in 14s, evicted after 2 windows
[batcher] schedule_delay_ms=48
```

maria: that log snippet is typical. bursts are short (1–10 requests) but frequent for some tenants. eviction after just 2 windows is too aggressive.

tia: operationally, safer to make defaults conservative. can still expose aggressive knobs for customers who want tighter tail latency/cost.

lee: question: do we want deprioritization to reduce batch weight or to physically move tenant to a low-prio queue? difference matters for fairness accounting.

sam: I'd prefer leaving tenant in same queue but with a credit multiplier. moving queues complicates lane fencing and KV locality.

jon: lane fencing + queue shuffles cause lock contention. soft credits are simpler: decrease token consumption per request until tenant recovers.

maria: new idea — add a short-lived "protected KV" state that survives N windows but is trimmed at object granularity instead of full evict. trim LRU keys first. keeps hot prefixes.

tia: trimming LRU keys sounds promising. Does runtime expose per-tenant LRU metrics?

lee: we have per-tenant key counts and last-access histograms in telemetry. could expose a cheap LRU epoch marker.

maria: ok action items: (1) prototype hysteresis counter + soft-deprio (maria/sam), (2) add eviction alignment to coalesce tick and expose config (lee), (3) explore protected-KV LRU-trim in runtime (jon). i'll open a tracking PR and link in here.

infra-bot: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/coalescer/pull/421 — 'hysteresis-soft-deprio-eviction-alignment'

sam: i'll add unit tests around repeated bursts and ensure metrics show decreased rehydrate events.

jon: let's also run a canary with mixed tenant traffic (bursty + steady) to measure impact on throughput and 99th pct.

maria: thanks all. one more: include a conservatively high default for eviction_grace_windows so we don't surprise prod. we can doc the perf/memory tradeoff in the PR description. :memo:
